Case N04: segment the peripheral nerve sheath tumor on this T2-weighted MRI.

Volume: 121x121x111 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.
final_assistant_text:
Segmentation complete for case N04.

**Result:** One peripheral nerve sheath tumor segmented on the T2-weighted MRI — a 5.6 mL, single-component mass centered in the thigh adjacent to the femur.

**Process:**
- Located the hyperintense mass on axial (k≈64–103), coronal (j≈53–70) and sagittal (i≈36–54) sheets.
- Seeded with a positive point inside the lesion at axial 85 → initial mask captured the bright core with tapered cranio-caudal ends.
- The model's boundary was stable under refinement (Δ ≈ −0.1 mL); no intensity-based candidate corrections were proposed.
- Verified the boundary at the superior end (axial 65–75), mid-level (axial 84–85/90), and inferior end (axial 93–100), plus coronal (56/60/62) and sagittal (44/46) planes; adjacent linear bright structures were vessels/fascia, correctly excluded.
- Final review (five slices per plane) confirmed no lesion tissue beyond the mask ends and no stray components.

**Confidence: medium** — boundary is clearly correct for the solid hyperintense mass in all three planes; only the very faint tapered periphery at the extreme ends is somewhat ambiguous.
